corpus.title: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as Middle East conflict deepens
corpus.signal_text:
Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East conflict expanded.
Riyadh struck Houthi military targets in Hodeida on Friday, with rebel media reporting two wounded after the Yemeni group announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hit its ships.
The flare-up marks a new front of the war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.
The rebels had accused Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” and said its actions “will not go unanswered”.
The Houthis’ Ansarollah media said on Telegram early on Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan on the Red Sea.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.
But Riyadh’s civil defence agency had issued brief warnings to residents in Jizan and Yanbu early Saturday for “potential danger”, only to lift the warnings minutes later.
Similar warnings have been issued in the past when missiles or drones were fired at the kingdom.
The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.
A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.
The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.
Blockade
The Yemeni security source, who requested anonymity, said the Saudi strikes targeted a telecommunications building near Hodeida’s port and a naval base at Ras al-Kathib in Hodeida.
The Houthis’ al-Masirah television channel said two people were wounded — a worker in Hodeida and a woman on Kamaran island.
It said a telecoms building had been hit in Hodeida.
On Monday, the rebels had warned in a radio message to ships that they would target vessels “belonging to (the) Saudi enemy” that do not comply with their blockade.
Saudi state media cited a transport authority official on Friday as saying “the vessel (NCC MASA), belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea today … resulting in minor damage to the vessel’s hull”.

Sanaa – Tehran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabia on Saturday as US President Donald Trump mulled fresh strikes on Iran in the deepening Middle East war.
The US military broke its daily announcement of fresh strikes on the Islamic republic on Saturday, following 13 nights in a row hitting military targets there.
Trump said he had not yet decided whether to launch major strikes on Iran, hours before the conflict widened across the region with Yemen’s Houthi rebels claiming a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan.
The Houthis had accused US ally Riyadh of a “dangerous escalation” after it struck military targets belonging to the group on Friday, following the rebels announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.
The flare-up marks a new front in a war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.
Riyadh did not immediately comment on the Houthis’ Ansarollah media post on Telegram on Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in Jizan.
But Riyadh’s civil defence agency issued brief warnings to residents in the city, as well as Yanbu, early on Saturday.
The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.
A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.
The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

The escalation came after Trump said he would hold off on a major operation as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.

corpus.title: Iran-Backed Houthis Claim Missile Strike On Saudi Arabia
corpus.signal_text:
Houthis Claim Strike On Saudi Arabia After Riyadh Hits Yemen Targets
Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on July 25, hours after vowing to retaliate for Saudi air strikes on military targets in Yemen the previous day.
The Houthis' Ansarollah media said a "Yemeni missile strike" sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan, while Riyadh issued and quickly lifted civil defense warnings for Jizan and Yanbu but made no immediate comment on the claim.
The escalation followed Saudi strikes on July 24 against Houthi military sites in Hodeida, including a naval base at Ras al-Kathib, a military camp on Kamaran island, and a telecommunications building near the port, according to a Yemeni security source.
Houthi media said two civilians were wounded. Riyadh said it had targeted sites threatening commercial shipping after the Yemeni rebels announced a blockade of Saudi shipping and attacked vessels in the Red Sea.
On July 20, the Houthis warned that they would target ships "belonging to (the) Saudi enemy" that ignored the blockade.
Earlier this week, they claimed attacks on two Saudi ships. On July 24, Saudi Arabia confirmed one Saudi-owned vessel, NCC MASA, sustained minor hull damage in the Red Sea but continued its voyage.
The escalation has sparked concerns about oil supplies, with Saudi Arabia increasingly reliant on Red Sea export routes with the war in Iran disrupting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
The latest exchange also raises the prospect of renewed cross-border fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, jeopardizing a de facto cease-fire that has largely held since a UN-brokered truce between the Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognized government expired in October 2022.
Saudi Arabia has backed Yemen's government against the Houthis since leading a military intervention in 2015, although cross-border hostilities have largely subsided in recent years.

Saudi-led coalition bombs Yemeni port (VIDEOS)
The Saudi-led coalition struck targets in the Houthi-held Yemeni port of Hodeidah on Saturday following attacks on Saudi ships in the Red Sea.
The Houthis, an Iranian-backed Shiite group that controls large parts of civil war-torn Yemen, announced a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia last week in response to what it called the unjust “siege” of the country.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki Al-Maliki said in a statement that the strikes targeted military sites used to “threaten commercial vessels.”
According to the Houthi-aligned Al Masirah TV, telecommunications facilities were hit. The broadcaster added that a woman was injured in a strike on Kamaran Island off Yemen’s Red Sea coast.
The group’s political wing condemned the attacks and vowed to meet “escalation with escalation,” according to Anadolu.

Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Tehran-allied Houthi movement edged closer to opening a new front in the Iran war overnight, after Riyadh bombed the port city of Hodeidah in retaliation for a Houthi missile strike on one of its ships in the Red Sea.
The exchange marks the latest escalation since the Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, imposed an embargo on Saudi shipping on Monday, disrupting maritime traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects Asia to Europe via the Suez Canal.
A near-identical Houthi missile attack on an oil tanker owned by the National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia on Thursday had already prompted threats of American military intervention from US President Donald Trump.
“If they do this again, the US will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a surrogate and/or proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The Houthis claimed a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan on Saturday, after media the group controls accused Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” and said its actions “will not go unanswered”.
Pakistan, which shares a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia, warned it would “take all necessary measures, including lawful use of force”, should its own “maritime interests” come under threat.
